newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss bank complaint names Arthur Andersen.
newsitem.headline: Swiss bank complaint names Arthur Andersen.

text.p: Swiss regional bank Solothurner Bank said Friday it filed a complaint that seeks damages against the Zurich office of international auditing and consulting concern Arthur Andersen.
The complaint was filed in the Zurich Court of Commerce in early March.
Arthur Andersen, in a separate statement, said it rejected the accusations.
The plaintiffs allege the auditing firm took improper care in its role in a takeover by Solothurner Cantonalbank of another bank, Bank in Kriegstetten, finalised in 1993.

"After the acquisition it was found that the value assessed by Arthur Andersen did not match the effective value of the Bank in Kriegstetten and millions (of Swiss francs) were needed for additional provisions," the Solothurner Bank said.
"Arthur Andersen has taken note of Solothurner Bank's complaint. The complaint contains no new elements," the firm saidn in rejecting the allegations.
It said that Solothurner Cantonalbank reached a decision to purchase Bank in Kriegstetten on May 16, 1992. It also said that its contract was at first limited to a "summary computation of value."
"The work did not include in any way or form a comprehensive evaluation, let alone a full audit," it said.
